members.name: Do dominant technology platforms' design choices and private governance practices determine privacy outcomes more than formal legal rules do?

themes.name: Are existing privacy protections adequate for employee data collection and workplace monitoring?
themes.definition: This question focuses on informational privacy, surveillance, and power asymmetries in employment relationships.

members.name: Are existing privacy protections adequate for employee data collection and workplace monitoring?

themes.name: Should specialized regulators and proactive organizational governance supplement case-by-case privacy enforcement?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether dedicated institutions, internal decision structures, audits, and preventive governance can manage data risks more effectively than litigation alone.

members.name: Should specialized regulators and proactive organizational governance supplement case-by-case privacy enforcement?

themes.name: Should privacy law address the physical-safety risks created by networked devices and connected infrastructures?
themes.definition: This question examines whether privacy and data-governance rules should cover harms arising when Internet-connected systems transform information practices into risks to bodily or environmental safety.

members.name: Should privacy law address the physical-safety risks created by networked devices and connected infrastructures?

themes.name: Should online platforms and nontraditional publishers bear different privacy obligations from conventional publishers when disseminating personal information?
themes.definition: This question addresses how legal responsibility for online disclosure, commercial persona, identity information, and reputational or privacy harms should vary across information intermediaries.

members.name: Should online platforms and nontraditional publishers bear different privacy obligations from conventional publishers when disseminating personal information?

themes.name: Should data-retention limits and lifecycle controls be mandatory for organizations that collect personal information?
themes.definition: This question asks whether restricting how long data may be stored and reused can reduce risks from later disclosure, aggregation, and unauthorized access.

members.name: Should data-retention limits and lifecycle controls be mandatory for organizations that collect personal information?

themes.name: Should courts expand common-law or constitutional privacy protections when legislation fails to address new forms of data collection and disclosure?
themes.definition: This question concerns the role of courts in adapting privacy torts, defining protected personhood and communication, and extending privacy rights beyond traditional state-action or physical-space limits.

members.name: Should courts expand common-law or constitutional privacy protections when legislation fails to address new forms of data collection and disclosure?

themes.name: How should law regulate facial recognition and other technologies that make individuals publicly identifiable?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether and under what conditions technologically enabled identification, tracking, or classification in public and semi-public spaces should be lawful.

members.name: How should law regulate facial recognition and other technologies that make individuals publicly identifiable?

themes.name: How should law regulate downstream data sharing among private entities while preserving useful information flows?
themes.definition: This question addresses whether purpose limitations, transfer restrictions, contractual controls, or other rules can govern data movement without eliminating socially or economically valuable uses.

members.name: How should law regulate downstream data sharing among private entities while preserving useful information flows?

themes.name: How should election-related transparency and enforcement be balanced against political privacy and anonymity?
themes.definition: This question concerns whether disclosure requirements and election oversight unjustifiably chill political participation or expose sensitive political activity.

members.name: How should election-related transparency and enforcement be balanced against political privacy and anonymity?

themes.name: How should U.S. privacy law respond to the GDPR's extraterritorial reach and its affirmative compliance duties?
themes.definition: This question examines the effects of European privacy requirements on U.S. organizations and the divergence between European and American models of data protection.

members.name: How should U.S. privacy law respond to the GDPR's extraterritorial reach and its affirmative compliance duties?

themes.name: Does the right to be forgotten unlawfully suppress truthful or legitimately public information?
themes.definition: This question examines whether deletion or delisting rights improperly restrict speech, public access, or the circulation of lawfully obtained information.

members.name: Does the right to be forgotten unlawfully suppress truthful or legitimately public information?

themes.name: Does cybersecurity adequately address privacy harms caused by digital systems and security interventions?
themes.definition: This question distinguishes protection against unauthorized access from broader harms caused by monitoring, data aggregation, disclosure, or security measures themselves.

members.name: Does cybersecurity adequately address privacy harms caused by digital systems and security interventions?

themes.name: Does HIPAA's institutional and rule-based model adequately protect individuals' health-information privacy?
themes.definition: This question assesses whether HIPAA's Privacy Rule sufficiently governs health-data collection, disclosure, secondary use, and individual control.

members.name: Does HIPAA's institutional and rule-based model adequately protect individuals' health-information privacy?

themes.name: Do privacy rules create incentives that unintentionally increase collection, disclosure, or surveillance?
themes.definition: This question analyzes whether legal requirements, market structures, and organizational practices designed to protect privacy can instead encourage additional data accumulation or monitoring.

members.name: Do privacy rules create incentives that unintentionally increase collection, disclosure, or surveillance?

themes.name: Do privacy protections for personally identifying information adequately address online identity theft and financial harm?
themes.definition: This question examines whether legal rules prevent unauthorized acquisition, disclosure, aggregation, and reuse of identifying data in ways that enable fraud or other concrete harms.

members.name: Do privacy protections for personally identifying information adequately address online identity theft and financial harm?

themes.name: Do consumer-facing procedures and increased enforcement measurably reduce privacy harms online?
themes.definition: This question calls for empirical evaluation of whether notices, consent interfaces, complaint systems, enforcement actions, and other interventions change behavior or reduce actual privacy-related harm.

members.name: Do consumer-facing procedures and increased enforcement measurably reduce privacy harms online?

themes.name: Do First Amendment doctrines unduly restrict remedies for technology-enabled privacy harms?
themes.definition: This question focuses on whether constitutional protections for speech and information dissemination prevent effective regulation of harmful disclosures and data practices.

members.name: Do First Amendment doctrines unduly restrict remedies for technology-enabled privacy harms?

themes.name: Can public disclosure and publicity effectively remedy organizational wrongdoing without creating disproportionate privacy harms?
themes.definition: This question evaluates disclosure as an accountability mechanism while considering retaliation, humiliation, exposure, and the privacy interests of affected individuals.

members.name: Can public disclosure and publicity effectively remedy organizational wrongdoing without creating disproportionate privacy harms?

themes.name: Can privacy torts provide better remedies for dignitary and psychological harms than defamation law?
themes.definition: This question evaluates whether civil privacy claims should recognize non-economic injuries arising from truthful publication, unwanted identification, exposure, or misuse of personal information.

members.name: Can privacy torts provide better remedies for dignitary and psychological harms than defamation law?

themes.name: Can government-controlled records and digital credentials improperly determine people's ability to exercise rights and participate in society?
themes.definition: This question investigates whether identification, authentication, and official record systems create privacy and autonomy risks by conditioning access to legal or social benefits.

members.name: Can government-controlled records and digital credentials improperly determine people's ability to exercise rights and participate in society?

themes.name: Can connected devices and pervasive sensors improve public safety without making privacy an unavoidable sacrifice?
themes.definition: This question investigates how networked technologies that interact with the physical world should be designed and regulated to reconcile security benefits with privacy risks.

members.name: Can connected devices and pervasive sensors improve public safety without making privacy an unavoidable sacrifice?

themes.name: Are sector-specific privacy laws adequate for data practices that cross institutional and technological boundaries?
themes.definition: This question tests whether protections organized around particular industries or information categories can govern data flows involving multiple sectors and private technology companies.

members.name: Are sector-specific privacy laws adequate for data practices that cross institutional and technological boundaries?

themes.name: Are biometric and identification technologies more effective as privacy safeguards or as tools of surveillance?
themes.definition: This question evaluates the circumstances in which identification systems can protect anonymity or security versus enabling persistent tracking and loss of privacy.

members.name: Are biometric and identification technologies more effective as privacy safeguards or as tools of surveillance?
